name: Ezer
overview: Ezer was a male Edomite chief known primarily as the son of Seir, a prominent figure in the Edomite lineage. His leadership role is noted in the genealogical records of Genesis, highlighting his significance within the tribe of Edom. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezer appears as a proper name in Scripture without a given meaning or divine attribution. It is simply recorded as the name of this Edomite leader in Genesis 36:21.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ezer as the son of Seir. Additional inferred paternal relationships suggest connections to Bilhan, Zaavan, Akan, and Jucam, indicating a broader family context within the Edomite chiefs. However, these are not directly stated but inferred from related genealogical listings.
scriptureSignificance: Ezer's significance lies in his role as a chief within the Edomite tribe, underscoring the established leadership structure among the descendants of Seir. His mention in Genesis 36 situates him within the biblical narrative as part of the Edomite heritage, which is important for understanding the broader context of Israel's neighboring peoples. Though not extensively detailed, his position as a leader reflects the organized tribal governance recognized in Scripture.
